additional_info.subject: Case creation Notes
additional_info.body: Today I got a message that the 170003777 was completely faulted. In SCB I saw that both plugs were deactivated so I gave a soft reboot around 08h48. This without any results. Our techs went on site to run some tests. The tech then did a reboot through the screen as recommended by Siemens. Also without any result. Since this did not help, they had to give the charger a hard reboot. Being to turn it completely off and on. This was around 9.30 am. Can you please check why the first two reboots did not work?

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0401458-DC/Si-D/BE-MP / S6 170003777] First two reboots did not work CRM:00642001963
additional_info.body:
Hello Chloë,
Hope you are doing great.
As far as we understand your query:
You rebooted the charger twice, but it didn't work. A technician then rebooted the charger on-site, and it worked well.
Could you please clarify what you mean by "the reboot did not work"?
In the context of OCPP, a soft reboot and a hard reboot refer to different ways of restarting a charging station EVSE:
Soft Reboot
:
Restarts the system without cutting off power to the charging station.
Involves restarting the software and services while maintaining hardware and electrical power.
Used to resolve software-related issues or apply configurations without affecting the power supply.
Less disruptive to ongoing charging sessions or connections.
Hard Reboot
:
Involves restarting the system by physically cutting off the power and then restoring it.
Reboots both the software and hardware.
More disruptive, may temporarily interrupt charging sessions, and the charge point may go offline.
Used when a soft reboot does not resolve an issue or to reset hardware components after a malfunction or electrical problem.
In OCPP terms
:
Soft Reboot: Usually a "Reset" command that only affects software and configurations.
Hard Reboot: Might be considered a "Reboot" or "Reset" command that affects the system more thoroughly, including hardware or power state.
The choice between a soft and hard reboot depends on the nature of the problem and the desired outcome. A soft reboot is less disruptive, while a hard reboot is more comprehensive and can fix deeper issues.
Thank you
Best Regards
eMobility Tech Support Team - Mohini
